شَوْلَةٌ The part that it raises of the tail of the scorpion; (S, O, K;) and so ↓ شَوْلٌ : (Ham p. 649:) or, accord. to Sh, its sting, with which it strikes. (TA.) ―
-b2- [Hence,] الشَّوْلَةُ (assumed tropical:) Two bright stars, near together, [ λ and ν ,] (S, O,) in the end of the tail of Scorpio, (Kzw,) which are one of the Mansions of the Moon, (S, O, Kzw,) namely, the Nineteenth Mansion; (Kzw;) also called حُمَةُ العَقْرَبِ. (S, O.) [See مَنَازِلُ القَمَرِ, in art. نزل.] ―
-b3- And شَوْلَةُ is a proper name for The scorpion; (O, TA;) [and] so ↓ شَوَّالَةُ . (K, TA.) ＝
-A2- Also A foolish, or stupid, woman. (IAar, O, K.) شَوْلَةُ was the name of A certain foolish female slave, belonging to [the tribe of] 'Adwán, and she used to give advice to her masters, and it resulted in evil to them; whence the saying, أَنْتَ شَوْلَةُ النَّاصِحَةُ [Thou art Showleh the giver of advice]. (S, O, K.) ―
-b2- Also the name of The mare of Zeyd-el-Fawáris Ed-Dabbee. (O, K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
